metadata.laymanSummary: House Ways & Means Committee examined what happens when 2017 Trump tax cuts expire in 2025 and heard testimony on their fiscal and economic impact.

data.billTitle: Hearing: The Coming Tax Cliff — Expiring TCJA Provisions and the Path Forward

speakers.name: Rep. Jim Jordan
speakers.title: R-OH · House Judiciary Chair
speakers.quote: If we do nothing, 90% of American taxpayers will see a tax increase in 2026. The standard deduction gets cut in half. The child tax credit drops from $2,000 to $1,000. This is not a tax debate — this is a family budget emergency that Congress created and Congress must fix.

speakers.name: Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez
speakers.title: D-NY · House Oversight
speakers.quote: Extending the TCJA fully would add $3.7 trillion to the national debt over ten years. We should absolutely protect the middle-class provisions — but the top-bracket cuts that primarily benefit millionaires and billionaires should expire as scheduled. We don't need to borrow from our children to cut taxes for people who don't need it.

speakers.name: Rep. Hakeem Jeffries
speakers.title: D-NY · House Minority Leader
speakers.quote: Democrats have been consistent: protect working families from a tax increase. Extend the middle-class provisions. Let the provisions that benefit only the ultra-wealthy expire. A deal is available if Republicans are willing to negotiate instead of demanding a full extension that benefits their donors.

data.title: About This Hearing
data.text: The House Ways and Means Committee heard testimony from the CBO Director, Treasury Department officials, and outside economists on May 7, 2026 regarding the expiration of 23 TCJA provisions. If Congress does not act, the standard deduction reverts from $14,600 to $7,550, the top marginal rate increases from 37% to 39.6%, and the estate tax exemption drops from $13.6M to $6.8M.
